description: 100 golden test cases for MaterialGenesis evaluation suite covering 14 material domains

test_cases.request: Design a sodium-ion battery anode composite using hard carbon as active material with 80 wt% loading. Include 8 wt% conductive carbon black, 7 wt% sodium-compatible binder, and 5 wt% porosity modifiers. Target specific capacity >300 mAh/g, coulombic efficiency >98%, rate capability 2C, cycling >200 cycles at 50-80°C. Provide composition, processing method, characterization plan, and validation targets.

Develop a lithium-ion battery cathode material with high nickel content. Include methods for sol-gel synthesis, calcination parameters (700-800°C), doping with Al, Mg, or Co, and cycling performance validation up to 500 cycles. What composition and characterization methods ensure structural stability and prevent oxygen loss?

Create a solid-state battery electrolyte using polymer matrix with ceramic filler. Target ionic conductivity >10^-4 S/cm at 60°C, electrochemical stability window >5V, and mechanical strength for cycling. Include processing method, characterization techniques (EIS, SEM, XRD), and validation metrics.

Design a potassium-ion battery anode using graphite or hard carbon. Requirements: initial capacity >300 mAh/g, coulombic efficiency >95%, cycling >100 cycles, pre-sodiation or pre-potassiation method to improve first-cycle efficiency. Specify materials, processing, and validation approach.

Develop a dual-carbon anode for sodium-ion batteries combining hard carbon (dominant) with some graphite. Target 250-300 mAh/g, optimize for low-cost production, cycling stability >500 cycles, and safety. Include pre-treatment of graphite, blending ratios, heat treatment parameters, and post-lithiation/sodiation.

Create a silicon-dominant lithium-ion anode combining Si (active) with graphite (buffer). Address volume expansion cycling, pre-lithiation, and SEI formation. Target capacity >1000 mAh/g, coulombic efficiency >98%, cycling >300 cycles at C/5 rate. Processing: mechanical mixing, thermal treatment, coating methods.

Design a manganese oxide (MnOx) cathode for aqueous zinc-ion batteries with high capacity, low cost, and environmental safety. Target capacity >300 mAh/g, discharge voltage >1.2V, cycling >1000 cycles in aqueous electrolyte. Include material synthesis, manganese precursors, calcination, dopants (Ca, Co, Fe), and validation approach.

Develop a nickel-rich layered oxide cathode (NCA or NCM90) with doping and coating for high-energy lithium-ion batteries. Address structural instability, oxygen loss, and cation mixing. Include sol-gel or solid-state synthesis, calcination profiles (700-900°C), Al/Mg doping levels, and coating materials (Al2O3, ZrO2, SiO2).

Create a zinc-air battery anode using zinc powder, alloy additives (Pb, In, Ca, Al), and gel electrolytes. Target discharge capacity >400 mAh/cm², cycle life >100 cycles, low self-discharge. Include zinc particle size control, alloy ratios, corrosion inhibitors (triethylenediamine, benzotriazole), and validation metrics.

Design a lithium metal anode for next-generation batteries with high capacity density. Address dendrite formation, cycling efficiency >99.5%, and electrolyte compatibility. Include lithium metal source, surface treatments (graphene, AI2O3 coating), electrolyte additives (LiNO3, cinnamaldehyde), and characterization methods (plating/stripping, morphology, impedance).

Develop an adsorbent material for phosphate recovery from agricultural wastewater. Composition: calcium hydroxide-based minerals, iron oxide phosphate binders. Target orthophosphate (PO4-P) recovery 60-80% at pH 5-9, adsorption capacity >20 mg PO4-P/g adsorbent, 5-10 regeneration cycles via pH swing or salt desorption. Include nutrient release testing for fertilizer reuse.

Design a phosphate recovery material for industrial wastewater using layered double hydroxides (LDH) or metal-organic frameworks (MOF). Target high selectivity for phosphate over competing ions (NO3-, SO4-2, Cl-), pH-dependent binding for reversible adsorption, and 10+ cycling stability. Include synthesis method, characterization (XRD, BET, SEM/EDS), and regeneration efficiency metrics.

Create a phosphate-selective ion exchange resin for nutrient recovery. Specify amine-functionalized polymer backbone, phosphate binding groups, pH range 4-8, capacity >100 mg P/mL resin, and regeneration using alkaline solutions (pH >11) or salt gradients. Include cycling stability >50 cycles and environmental sustainability assessment.

Develop a biochar-based phosphate adsorbent incorporating iron oxides and aluminum compounds. Source: agricultural residue biochar (rice husk, straw) with Fe(OH)3 or Al2O3 loading. Target PO4-P removal >70% from phosphate-rich manure or municipal wastewater, adsorption capacity >15 mg/g, regeneration via 0.1-1M NaOH or HCl.

Design a phosphate recovery system for swine manure slurry using apatite (Ca5(PO4)3X) or phosphate-binding minerals. Composition: calcium silicate or magnesium compound with phosphate binders. Target removal >80% of dissolved and colloidal phosphorus, product recovery as nutrient salt for fertilizer formulation, and cost <$0.50 per kg treated.

Create a dual-functional adsorbent for simultaneous phosphate and nitrogen recovery from wastewater. Combine phosphate-selective binding sites with nitrogen-binding groups (e.g., carbon nitrides, N-doped materials). Target P recovery >60%, N recovery >50%, regeneration via pH swing or solvent extraction, and reusability >10 cycles.

Develop a hybrid adsorbent combining activated carbon with iron-aluminum hydroxide precipitate for wastewater polishing. Target orthophosphate (PO4-P) adsorption >90%, polyphosphate conversion via hydrolysis, and treatment cost <$0.30/m³. Include material synthesis, regeneration efficiency, and lifecycle assessment for nutrient-rich sludge reuse.

Design an amine-functionalized sorbent for CO2 capture from flue gas (10-15% CO2, 60-80°C). Composition: porous silica or resin backbone with primary amine loading (2-4 mmol/g). Target CO2 capacity >2 mmol/g at 75°C, rapid kinetics (<30 min), and 50+ regeneration cycles at 100-120°C. Include breakthrough analysis and energy cost calculation.

Create a direct air capture (DAC) material targeting 400 ppm CO2 from ambient air. Specify moisture-tolerant amine or alkaline sorbent, handling of humidity (40-60% RH), and regeneration at moderate temperature (60-80°C). Target CO2 uptake >1 mmol/g, cycling >1000 times, and cost-effective moisture swing or temperature swing.

Develop a metal-organic framework (MOF) for CO2 separation with high selectivity over N2. Target CO2/N2 selectivity >20, CO2 capacity >10 mmol/g, and stability in humid flue gas (10% water vapor). Include framework composition (Zn, Cu, Al nodes), organic linker selection, and testing at 25°C and 75°C.

Design a zeolite-based CO2 sorbent for post-combustion capture from coal/natural gas power plants. Composition: 13X or 5A zeolite with hydrophobic coatings (silane treatment) to resist moisture. Target CO2 capacity >4 mmol/g, N2 capacity <0.5 mmol/g at 40°C, thermal stability to 300°C, and regeneration via vacuum or steam.

Create a carbon-based sorbent (activated carbon, graphene oxide) functionalized with amino groups for CO2 capture. Target CO2 capacity >5 mmol/g, rapid uptake kinetics, operating temperature 25-75°C, and low regeneration cost (70-100°C). Include surface area optimization (>1000 m²/g), pore size engineering, and environmental assessment.

Develop a humidity-swing adsorbent for CO2 capture using moisture-responsive polymers or inorganic hydrates. Mechanism: CO2 absorption increases with increasing humidity up to ~40% RH, then reverses at low humidity for regeneration. Target CO2 working capacity >1.5 mmol/g, cycling >100 times, minimal energy input (humidity control only).

Design a supported ionic liquid (SIL) for selective CO2 capture from natural gas or biogas (5% CO2, balance CH4/N2). Composition: ionic liquid imidazolium or phosphonium on porous silica support. Target CO2/CH4 selectivity >10, CO2 loading >0.5 mol/kg, cycling >50 times at 25-40°C, and regeneration via vacuum or thermal swing.

Create a produced-water pre-treatment media for ADNOC oilfield operations. Handle hot, high-salinity Gulf conditions (50-80°C, 50-100 g/L TDS). Remove oil/grease, hydrocarbons (>95% removal), sulfide compounds, and fine solids. Backwash characteristics: pressure <2 bar, recovery >85%. Compatibility with downstream membrane filters and secondary treatment.

Develop an adsorbent material for BTEX removal (benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, xylene) from produced water. Composition: activated carbon with hydrophobic coating or polymeric resin. Target BTEX removal >90%, adsorption capacity >100 mg/g, operating temperature 20-80°C, and regeneration via steam stripping or solvent extraction.

Design a coalescer media for water-oil separation in produced water treatment. Composition: oleophilic, hydrophobic porous material (e.g., polypropylene, polyurethane, or graphene foam). Target oil droplet coalescence to >20 µm, oil removal efficiency >95%, pressure drop <0.5 bar, and lifetime >1000 hours at 5-50 m/h flow rate.

Create an ion-exchange resin for produced-water desalination targeting TDS reduction from 50-100 g/L to <5 g/L. Specify cation and anion exchanger types, regeneration frequency, operating temperature (20-60°C), and disposal of regenerant brines. Target throughput >10 bed volumes per cycle.

Develop a sulfide oxidation catalyst for produced-water treatment preventing H2S odor and toxicity. Composition: iron oxide or manganese oxide particles on porous support. Target H2S removal >99%, catalyst lifespan >6 months, operating temperature 25-80°C, and regeneration via air oxidation.

Design a scale-inhibitor media for produced-water reinjection preventing calcite, barite, or sulfate salt deposition in injection wells. Composition: polymeric scale inhibitor on inert support or chelating resin. Target inhibition of >95% scale formation, operating temperature 50-100°C, and compatibility with high-salinity brine.

Create a multi-stage produced-water treatment system combining physical separation (settling, coalescing), chemical treatment (oxidation, precipitation), and polishing (adsorption/ion exchange). Specify each stage's media, target outlet water quality (TOC <50 mg/L, oil <5 mg/L), and total treatment cost per m³.

Develop a pretreatment media for seawater reverse osmosis (RO) desalination. Remove turbidity, suspended solids, colloids, and biofouling precursors. Composition: multimedia filter (sand, anthracite, activated carbon). Target silt density index (SDI) <3, turbidity <0.5 NTU, operating flux 15-20 m/h, backwash frequency every 24-48 hours.

Create a cartridge filter media for seawater intake pretreatment targeting particle size 50-100 µm removal. Composition: depth-type polyester or polypropylene with gradient density. Target flow rate >50 m³/h/m², pressure drop <0.5 bar, dirt-holding capacity >500 g/m², and replacement interval 3-6 months.

Design a granular activated carbon (GAC) filter for seawater organics removal (DOC, color, taste, odor). Target organic removal >80%, contact time >10 min, backwash frequency <4 times/day, and EBCT 10-15 min. Include carbon specifications (iodine number, density) and regeneration schedule.

Develop a coagulation/flocculation pretreatment media using ferric chloride or aluminum sulfate as coagulants. Target turbidity reduction to <1 NTU, particle size growth to >10 µm for effective settling, and residual iron/aluminum <0.5 mg/L. Include pH adjustment, dosing, retention time, and clarifier design.

Create a biofouling prevention media for seawater intake using antifouling coatings or biocidal additives. Composition: copper oxide (CuO) or silver nanoparticles on porous support. Target biofilm inhibition >90%, effective lifespan >6 months, and minimal heavy metal leaching to treated water.

Design an iron-manganese oxidation media for seawater trace contaminant removal (arsenic, selenium, heavy metals). Composition: green sand (glauconite) or zeolite with manganese oxide coating. Target As <10 µg/L outlet, contact time 15-20 min, and regeneration via air oxidation.

Develop an oil/fuel spill response media for seawater intake protection. Composition: oleophilic porous material (recycled plastic foam, polypropylene) that preferentially absorbs hydrocarbons >95%, resists water absorption. Target absorption capacity >500% by weight, pressurization tolerance >5 bar, and disposal as solid waste.

Design a fabric oil-stain removal composite for laundry/dry-cleaning applications. Composition: surfactant-loaded porous matrix, lipophilic nanoparticles, enzymatic additives. Target: >90% oil stain removal in <1 hour pre-soak at 40-60°C, water-based or low-VOC solvent formulation, color stability of treated fabrics (fading <5 AATCC units). Include safety for multiple fabric types (cotton, polyester, wool).

Create a biodegradable enzyme-based stain remover for organic soil (grass, coffee, blood, sweat) on textiles. Specify protease, amylase, and lipase enzyme types, optimal pH 5-8, temperature 30-60°C, and washing compatibility with modern detergents. Target stain removal >85% without fiber damage.

Develop a soil-release finish for synthetic fabrics preventing oil/stain adhesion. Composition: hydrophilic polymer coating on polyester or nylon. Target: contact angle increase to >80° (oil resistant), low add-on weight (<1% w/w), durability through 10+ wash cycles, and compatibility with dyes.

Design a stain-resistant textile treatment using fluorocarbon or silicone chemistry. Composition: PTFE or silicone polymer applied as finish or coating. Target: water/oil repellency (AATCC 118 spray test >80), durability >5 dry cleaning cycles or >20 home laundry cycles, reduced chemical migration to skin.

Create a grease-cutting laundry additive using lipase enzymes and surfactants. Composition: lipase enzyme (5-10 U/mL), non-ionic surfactants, chelating agents. Target: >80% grease removal from cotton workwear (machine washable, 60°C), enzyme stability through pre-wash soak, compatibility with chlorine bleach (low chlorine stability preferred).

Develop a mechanical/chemical hybrid fabric cleaning method using ultrasonic vibration + surfactant micelles. Specify frequency (20-40 kHz), power (5-20 W/L), contact time, and detergent type. Target: >85% removal of particulate and oily soil, reduced fabric wear vs. hand scrubbing, and low energy consumption.

Design an eco-friendly fabric stain remover using plant-based surfactants and essential oils. Composition: saponin extract, limonene (from citrus peel), enzymes. Target: >80% stain removal on cotton/wool blends, safe on delicate fabrics, biodegradable >90% OECD 301, and pleasant scent without synthetic fragrances.

Create a roof waterproofing and thermal insulation coating for concrete/asphalt surfaces in hot climates (50-80°C ambient). Composition: elastomeric polymer (acrylonitrile butadiene or polyurethane) with high solar reflectance (LSR >0.65), thermal resistance R-value >1 m²K/W, flame rating Class A. Application: brush or spray, 2-3 mm thickness.

Develop a cool roof coating using mineral-based pigments for urban heat island mitigation. Composition: acrylic or silicate binder with titanium dioxide (TiO2), alumina (Al2O3), reflective glass spheres. Target: solar reflectance >0.70, emissivity >0.85, surface temperature reduction >10°C vs. standard black roof, and durability >10 years.

Design a self-healing roof coating using microencapsulated healing agents (epoxy, polyurethane) or reversible polymer chemistry. Target: automatic crack healing for defects <0.5 mm within 24 hours, maintained waterproofing after 5-10 healing cycles, and compatibility with UV exposure.

Create a green roof thermal insulation system combining waterproofing membrane with root-resistant and drainage layers. Composition: EPDM or TPO waterproofing sheet, non-woven geotextile, recycled plastic drainage core, and lightweight growing substrate. Target: waterproofing >99.9%, root protection >25 years, thermal resistance R-2 m²K/W.

Develop a liquid-applied roof membrane using silicone or polyurethane chemistry. Composition: 2-part polyol + isocyanate (PU) or silicone elastomer. Target: application by spray/roller, 3-5 mm final thickness, waterproofing >99%, UV stability >15 years, and flexibility at -30 to +60°C.

Design a photocatalytic roof coating combining waterproofing with dirt/pollutant self-cleaning. Composition: acrylic polymer + TiO2 photocatalyst (3-5 wt%). Target: waterproofing >99%, TiO2 activity for dirt/algae degradation, maintained reflectance >60% after weathering, and durability >10 years.

Create a multi-layer thermal insulation and waterproofing system for extreme climates. Composition: polyiso or XPS foam core (R-4 m²K/W minimum), air barrier (kraft paper or plastic), reflective vapor retarder, and waterproofing topcoat. Target: thermal resistance R>6 m²K/W combined, waterproofing >99.9%, wind load resistance >150 km/h.

Design a hygroscopic salt-based atmospheric water harvesting material. Composition: lithium chloride (LiCl), calcium chloride (CaCl2), or potassium formate on porous silica or MOF support. Target: water uptake >1 kg H2O/kg sorbent at 30-50% RH, desorption temperature 60-80°C, cycling stability >100 cycles, and salt leaching <1% by mass per cycle.

Create a metal-organic framework (MOF) for water vapor capture from ambient air (30-60% RH). Specify framework composition (Zn, Al, Cr, Fe nodes), organic linker (imidazolate, triazolate, or hydroxyl-functionalized), and water uptake capacity. Target: >0.2 kg H2O/kg MOF at 40% RH, fast kinetics (<30 min), desorption at <80°C, and cycling >50 times.

Develop a polymer-based sorbent for atmospheric water harvesting using super-absorbent polymers (SAP) or polyelectrolyte complexes. Composition: crosslinked polyacrylic acid or polyethylene oxide with hygroscopic salts. Target: water uptake 2-3 kg H2O/kg sorbent at 50% RH, gentle heating (50-70°C) for desorption, reusability >50 cycles, and low cost (<$5/kg).

Design a passive radiative cooling + water harvesting composite for desert/arid regions. Combination: low-emissivity substrate achieving surface temperature <ambient at night, covered with water-sorbing layer. Target: nighttime surface temperature 5-10°C below ambient, water collection >0.1 kg/m²/night at 30% RH, and no energy input.

Create a desiccant wheel system for atmospheric water harvesting combining air dehumidification with water recovery. Composition: molecular sieve (3A or 5A zeolite) or silica gel on honeycomb rotor. Target: water extraction from 60% RH to <30% RH outlet, rotational speed 10-20 RPM, thermal efficiency >70%, and low maintenance.

Develop a bio-inspired water harvesting surface mimicking desert beetles or spider silk geometry. Composition: textured polymer or hydrogel with alternating hydrophobic-hydrophilic microsurfaces. Target: passive water collection >0.5 kg/m²/day at 60% RH without energy, self-cleaning via surface roughness, and durability >5 years outdoor exposure.

Design an ion-exchange resin-based water harvesting system for high-humidity environments (>70% RH). Composition: anion or cation exchange resin pre-loaded with hygroscopic salts. Target: water uptake >1.5 kg H2O/kg resin at 70% RH, desorption via gentle heating (50-60°C), cycling >100 times, and low salt leaching.

Create a TiO2-based photocatalytic coating for water treatment under UV/visible light. Composition: anatase or rutile TiO2 nanoparticles (20-100 nm) on porous support, doped with N, S, or Fe for visible-light activity. Target: pollutant degradation (dyes, organic compounds) >80% at 90 min under specified light, catalyst stability >50 cycles, and leaching <5% by mass.

Develop a graphene oxide (GO) + TiO2 composite photocatalyst for enhanced water pollutant degradation. Composition: GO as electron acceptor, TiO2 as photocatalyst. Target: pollutant removal >90% under UV/vis, visible-light activity (>400 nm), cycling stability >20 times, and cost-effective synthesis.

Design a bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) photocatalyst for visible-light water splitting and pollutant degradation. Target: visible-light activity (>420 nm), water splitting efficiency >2% under 1 sun, and photocatalytic degradation of organic dyes >70% within 2 hours.

Create a plasmonic photocatalyst using gold (Au) or silver (Ag) nanoparticles on TiO2 for enhanced visible-light activity. Composition: Au/Ag NPs (5-50 nm) on anatase TiO2. Target: enhanced visible-light absorption via localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), pollutant degradation >80%, and cycling stability >30 times.

Develop a heterojunction photocatalyst (e.g., TiO2/WO3, g-C3N4/BiVO4) for efficient charge separation and pollutant removal. Composition: two semiconductors with matched band gaps. Target: improved quantum efficiency >5% for visible-light, pollutant degradation >85% within 3 hours, and durability >50 cycles.

Design a photocatalytic membrane for continuous water purification combining photocatalysis with physical filtration. Composition: TiO2 or BiVO4 nanoparticles embedded in polymer membrane (PVDF, PES). Target: pollutant removal >90%, water flux >50 L/m²·h, and catalyst retention >99% (no leaching).

Create a Z-scheme photocatalyst system (e.g., BiVO4/graphene/g-C3N4) for enhanced water treatment under visible light. Composition: 3-phase system with electron mediator (graphene, Ag, or ionic liquid). Target: pollutant degradation >90% at 2 hours, dual oxidation pathways (·OH and ·O2- radicals), and cycling stability >50 times.

Create a self-cleaning building coating using TiO2 photocatalyst with hydrophilic surface. Composition: anatase TiO2 nanoparticles (UV-active) on exterior coating. Target: organic dirt/algae degradation via photocatalysis, enhanced water wetting (contact angle <30°), dirt wash-off in rain, and durability >10 years with minimal maintenance.

Design a superhydrophobic self-cleaning coating using nanostructured surfaces (e.g., SiO2 or TiO2 nanoparticles) with low-surface-energy polymers. Target: water contact angle >150°, dirt particles roll-off at <5° inclination, UV-stability >5 years, and flame resistance Class A.

Develop a biocidal self-cleaning coating using antimicrobial nanoparticles (silver, copper, or zinc oxide). Composition: Ag/Cu/ZnO nanoparticles on polymer matrix with low leaching. Target: bacterial growth inhibition >99% (ASTM G21), fungal resistance, reduced biofilm formation on building facades, and minimal environmental impact.

Create a hybrid self-cleaning coating combining photocatalytic (TiO2) and superhydrophobic (nanostructure) properties. Composition: TiO2 nanoparticles for photocatalysis + hydrophobic silane coupling agents. Target: UV-driven organic dirt degradation + water shedding, color stability >5 years, and weathering resistance ASTM G85.

Design a lotus-leaf-inspired self-cleaning facade coating using surface mimicry. Composition: textured polymer or epoxy with micro/nano-scale roughness (lotus-leaf structure). Target: superhydrophobic (>150° contact angle), dirt roll-off, reduced maintenance frequency, and aesthetic appeal for modern buildings.

Create a smart self-cleaning coating with switchable wettability (superhydrophobic ↔ hydrophilic) controlled by light or temperature. Composition: azobenzene-based or phase-change polymer with photocatalytic TiO2. Target: switching cycle <1 min, 100+ cycles, and automated dirt removal via triggered wettability change.

Develop a self-cleaning coating for transparent building materials (glass, polycarbonate) maintaining optical clarity. Composition: TiO2 nanocrystals in clear epoxy or acrylic binder. Target: optical clarity >90% transmission, photocatalytic activity >80%, and UV-stability >10 years on building windows.

Design a heavy metal adsorbent for lead (Pb2+), cadmium (Cd2+), and zinc (Zn2+) removal from contaminated water. Composition: activated carbon with chelating functional groups (-COOH, -NH2, -SH). Target: Pb removal >95%, Cd >90%, Zn >85% at pH 5-7, adsorption capacity >50 mg/g, and regeneration via acid elution.

Create a chitosan-based adsorbent for arsenic (As3+/As5+) and chromium (Cr6+) removal. Composition: chitosan polymer with amino and hydroxyl groups. Target: As removal >90%, Cr6+ removal >95% at pH 4-7, adsorption capacity >100 mg/g, and cost <$2/kg.

Develop an iron oxide (Fe2O3, Fe3O4) nanoparticle adsorbent for arsenite (As3+) and arsenate (As5+) removal. Composition: hematite or magnetite nanoparticles (10-50 nm) with surface hydroxyl groups. Target: As removal >99%, fast kinetics (<30 min), pH range 4-8, magnetic separation, and cycling >10 times.

Design a thiol-functionalized silica adsorbent for mercury (Hg2+) and gold (Au3+) removal. Composition: silica gel with thiol (-SH) grafted groups. Target: Hg removal >99%, Au removal >95%, adsorption capacity >200 mg/g Hg, cycling >50 times, and pH 3-8 operation.

Create a metal-organic framework (MOF) adsorbent for selective heavy metal capture. Composition: Zn or Cu-based MOF with N-containing organic linker. Target: high selectivity for Pb/Cd over Na/Ca, fast kinetics, reusability >20 cycles, and low cost synthesis.

Develop a graphene oxide (GO) composite for multi-pollutant heavy metal removal including Pb, Cd, Zn, Cr, and As. Composition: GO with coating of iron oxide or polymeric chelators. Target: >90% removal for all target metals, adsorption capacity >300 mg/g, and cycling stability >30 times.

Design a biochar-based adsorbent for radionuclide removal (uranium, thorium) and heavy metals from mining or nuclear wastewater. Composition: agricultural waste-derived biochar with phosphate or carboxylate modification. Target: U removal >95%, fast kinetics, reusability >20 cycles, and environmental safety.

Create a potassium-selective ion exchange resin for K+ recovery from mineral brines. Composition: ion-exchange resin with selective binding groups (crown ether, dibenzo-18-crown-6 or similar). Target: K+/Na+ selectivity >50, K+ recovery >80%, cycling >100 times, and regeneration via high-concentration KCl.

Develop a potassium-selective adsorbent using zeolites or layered double hydroxides (LDH). Composition: clinoptilolite zeolite or LDH with framework tuning for K+ selectivity. Target: K+ uptake >100 mg/g, K+/Na+ selectivity >30, adsorption from brines with 50-200 g/L Na+.

Design a solvent extraction system for potassium separation from brines using ionic liquids (IL). Composition: ionic liquid (e.g., imidazolium-based) with K+ complexing agent. Target: K+ extraction efficiency >85%, complete recovery via aqueous back-extraction, and IL recyclability >50 cycles.

Create a potassium-selective membrane for brine treatment. Composition: polymer membrane with selective K+ channels (synthetic or protein-based). Target: K+ flux >10 mol/m²·h, K+/Na+ selectivity >100, membrane durability >1000 h, and compatibility with high-salinity brines.

Develop a potassium recovery from Dead Sea or mineral-rich lake brines using crystallization technology. Composition: evaporative crystallization with impurity separation. Target: potassium chloride (KCl) or potassium sulfate (K2SO4) purity >99%, recovery >75%, and cost <$0.30/kg K2SO4.

Design a nano-adsorbent for potassium separation combining high surface area with K+ selectivity. Composition: nanostructured carbon (MOF, graphene, or zeolite nanoparticles) with K+ binding sites. Target: K+ adsorption capacity >200 mg/g, fast kinetics (<30 min), and magnetic or size-based separation.

Create an electrochemical potassium extraction system from brines using ion-selective electrodes. Composition: selective anode/cathode materials, potassium-selective separator membrane. Target: K+ recovery >80% at 100 A/m², high current efficiency, and low energy consumption (<5 kWh/kg K).

Design a reverse osmosis (RO) membrane for seawater desalination with high flux and low fouling. Composition: composite thin-film polyamide (TFP) membrane with surface modifications (antibiofouling coating). Target: water flux >20 L/m²·h, salt rejection >98%, membrane lifespan >5 years, and low biofouling rate.

Create an ultrafiltration (UF) membrane for wastewater treatment and reuse. Composition: polymer (PVDF or PES) with pore size 50-100 kDa MWCO. Target: turbidity removal >99%, suspended solids <1 NTU, high flux >100 L/m²·h, and cycling stability through multiple backwash cycles.

Design a nanofiltration (NF) membrane for softening and partial desalination of brackish water. Composition: polyamide or polysulfone with 1-2 nm pores. Target: divalent ion (Ca2+, Mg2+) rejection >90%, monovalent (Na+, Cl-) rejection 50-70%, and flux >15 L/m²·h.

Develop a forward osmosis (FO) membrane for low-energy wastewater treatment. Composition: asymmetric cellulose triacetate (CTA) or polyamide with selective layer support. Target: water flux >3-5 L/m²·h, salt rejection >99%, low internal concentration polarization (ICP), and compatibility with diverse feed solutions.

Create a microfiltration (MF) membrane for particle and bacterial removal from water. Composition: polypropylene or polyethersulfone with pore size 0.1-10 µm. Target: bacterial removal >99.99%, suspended solids removal >99%, high flux >200 L/m²·h, and easy backwashing.

Design a ceramic membrane for high-temperature and high-pH wastewater treatment. Composition: alumina (Al2O3), titania (TiO2), or zirconia (ZrO2) with thermal stability to 300°C. Target: pore size 50 nm (microfiltration grade), flux >50 L/m²·h, and compatibility with aggressive chemical cleaning.

Develop an ion-exchange membrane for desalination or separation applications. Composition: polymer backbone with cation-exchange groups (-SO3H, -COOH) or anion-exchange groups (-NR3+). Target: ion conductivity >0.01 S/cm, salt rejection >95%, mechanical strength through multiple cycles.

Design a closed-cell polyurethane foam for building thermal insulation. Composition: polyol + isocyanate reaction with blowing agent (HFC-245fa or cyclopentane). Target: thermal conductivity 0.020-0.025 W/m·K, compressive strength >100 kPa, flame rating Class B/C, and cost <$20/m³.

Create a mineral wool (fiberglass/rockwool) thermal insulation product with water resistance. Composition: inorganic fibers with hydrophobic binder and water-repellent coating. Target: thermal conductivity 0.030-0.040 W/m·K, water absorption <1% (after 24h soak), fire resistance Class A.

Design a phenolic foam insulation for high-temperature applications (up to 150°C continuous). Composition: phenolic resin with inorganic filler and blowing agent. Target: thermal conductivity 0.018-0.022 W/m·K, compressive strength >150 kPa at 10% deformation, flame rating Class A.

Develop an aerogel thermal insulation composite for extreme insulation needs. Composition: silica or polymer aerogel with reinforcement fibers. Target: ultra-low thermal conductivity <0.015 W/m·K, low density <100 kg/m³, and mechanical reinforcement for handling.

Create a vacuum insulation panel (VIP) for ultra-thin high-performance applications. Composition: porous core (fumed silica) in vacuum envelope (metallic barrier film). Target: effective thermal conductivity <0.004 W/m·K, panel thickness <20 mm, and pressure retention >5 years.

Design a composite thermal insulation board combining inorganic fibers and polymer binder for wall/roof applications. Composition: fiberglass/rockwool + phenolic or polyurethane binder. Target: thermal conductivity 0.025-0.035 W/m·K, compressive strength >50 kPa, and ease of installation.

Develop a bio-based thermal insulation material from agricultural waste (straw, wood fibers, cork). Composition: natural cellulosic fibers with bio-binder (starch, protein-based) or wax coating for water resistance. Target: thermal conductivity 0.040-0.060 W/m·K, sustainable/renewable source, and biodegradable end-of-life.

A custom material for high-performance space applications requiring extreme thermal cycling (-200 to +200°C), radiation resistance, and vacuum stability. Specify composition, synthesis method, and validation approach for multi-use space missions.
